bc_lower_hidden_walls.blurb: Lower Hidden Walls is a small group of cliffs in the New Crest Creek section of the Crest Creek Crags, inside Strathcona Provincial Park on Vancouver Island, a short drive from Gold River along Highway 28. It holds ten routes, a little over half of them trad and the rest bolted sport lines, on the basalt that characterizes this part of the island. Difficulty runs from easy fifth class up to low 5.11, with the bulk of the climbs sitting around 5.10. The walls stand among trees and stay cool and shaded, which makes them a good pick on a hot summer day. They are the first cliffs you meet when walking in from the lake area.
